decisions.rationale: Gengar+Tyranitar lead for Shadow Tag trap + Sand Stream; Excadrill back as Sand Rush sweeper hitting Metagross-Mega SE with High Horsepower and outspeeding everything under sand; Houndoom back as dedicated Serperior/Klefki answer (resists Grass, SE Flamethrower, Sucker Punch priority). decisions.notebook: Game 2: Brought Gengar/Tyranitar/Excadrill/Houndoom; left Gholdengo/Tauros on bench. Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag is primary wincon — prioritize keeping it healthy. decisions.rationale: Lead Dragapult + Rotom-Wash to handle both likely opponent leads. Against TTar+Excadrill: Dragapult Fire Blast into Excadrill (breaks Sash), Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump into TTar. Against Gengar+TTar: Dragapult Shadow Ball threatens Gengar, Rotom-Wash pressures TTar. Metagross in back threatens TTar and can OHKO Gengar with Psychic Fangs after Mega Evolving. Incineroar provides Intimidate cycling and Fake Out for mid-game tempo.

Dragapult Shadow Ball is a guaranteed OHKO on Gengar (110-165%) and Dragapult likely outspeeds Mega Gengar (213 vs ~199), so Gengar must Protect. Mega Evolving simultaneously gets Shadow Tag active this turn, trapping both foes. Tyranitar Crunch on Dragapult deals 58.5-108% (possible OHKO) — if Dragapult targets Gengar (blocked by Protect), this is a free heavy hit. Even worst case of double-target on Tyranitar (Thunderbolt 15-22% + Hydro Pump 46-70% ≈ 61-92%), TTar's 207 HP bulk likely survives. Next turn: Shadow Tag locks opponents in, Mega Gengar at full HP — primary wincon secured.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 Turn 1 plan: Gengar Protect+Mega for Shadow Tag, TTar Crunch Dragapult. Key damage notes: Dragapult Shadow Ball GUARANTEED OHKO on Gengar (110-165%). If Dragapult goes down, Rotom-Wash is trapped and Gengar Energy Ball handles it. Excadrill (280 Spe under sand) and Houndoom on bench for Serperior/Klefki if they appear.

decisions.rationale: Switch Dragapult to Incineroar before Gengar Mega Evolves and traps it with Shadow Tag. Incineroar's Intimidate weakens Tyranitar, and its Dark typing resists Gengar's Shadow Ball to only ~13-20% (even Helping Hand boosted ~21-30%). Rotom-Wash chips Gengar with Dark Pulse for 49-96%, putting it in KO range for later. This preserves Dragapult—my fastest mon and Gengar answer—while gaining board control with Incineroar's Fake Out threat next turn.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Incineroar Darkest Lariat is a guaranteed KO on Gengar (96-140%), so the opponent will almost certainly target Gengar to remove Shadow Tag. Gengar Protect (50% after consecutive use) is the only play that can potentially keep Shadow Tag active — if it works, it blocks Darkest Lariat, Dark Pulse, AND Parting Shot all targeting Gengar, while TTar Rock Slide chips both foes (SE on Incineroar 24-44%, neutral on Rotom) with flinch chance. If Protect fails, Gengar dies but TTar still gets Rock Slide damage — no worse than attacking and letting Gengar die. Switching Gengar out saves it but permanently loses Shadow Tag, and Houndoom has all-NVE matchups against both foes. The 50% coin flip for keeping the wincon active is the highest EV play.

decisions.rationale: Gengar-Mega's Shadow Tag traps both my Pokémon. The opponent's most lethal play is Helping Hand + Energy Ball from Tyranitar and Gengar into Rotom-Wash, which is a guaranteed KO. Rotom-Wash Protect (+4 priority) blocks that combo regardless of Gengar's speed advantage. Meanwhile, Incineroar's Darkest Lariat threatens Gengar-Mega for 73-142% — a strong chance to KO from 94%, especially since Gengar's consecutive Protect has only ~33% success. If Gengar does Protect successfully, we scout it and degrade its Protect further; Incineroar comfortably tanks Rock Slide (30-43%) and Shadow Ball (17-24%). This line covers both the aggressive Helping Hand + Energy Ball and the safe Protect + Rock Slide from the opponent.

This forces Protect, making it a dead Pokémon walking. Metagross Mega Evolves; Bullet Punch (+1 priority) outspeeds and KOs 4% Excadrill before it moves — Focus Sash only triggers from full HP. Rotom-Wash Hydro Pumps Tyranitar for 46–82%. This removes the Sand Rush sweeper without taking an attack from it, leaves Metagross-Mega healthy to answer Gengar-Mega with Psychic Fangs, and keeps Dragapult alive on the bench.

Both active Pokémon face guaranteed KOs: Excadrill (4%) dies to Metagross Bullet Punch priority, Tyranitar (38%) dies to Meteor Mash or Hydro Pump. Switching Excadrill to Houndoom brings in a Pokémon immune to Psychic Fangs and resistant to all Steel moves; the opponent's natural play (Bullet Punch on Excadrill's slot, Hydro Pump on Tyranitar) hits Houndoom for only 18-26% NVE and is blocked by Tyranitar's Protect. Next turn Houndoom Flamethrower (80-151% on Metagross) plus Tyranitar Crunch (29-50%) guarantees Metagross KO, leaving a 2v1 vs Rotom with Dragapult unable to attack at 15% HP.

Houndoom is the optimal switch-in vs Metagross: immune to Psychic Fangs (Dark-type), resists Meteor Mash/Bullet Punch (Fire resists Steel), only fears Rotom Hydro Pump (OHKO). Gengar-Mega is risky vs Metagross (Psychic Fangs guaranteed KO from 88%). Wincon: KO Metagross with Houndoom Flamethrower + Tyranitar Crunch, then clean up Rotom 2v1 while Dragapult sits uselessly. Tyranitar at -1 Atk still does 29-50% to Metagross with Crunch (SE). Sand has 4 turns remaining — sufficient for endgame without needing sandstream refresh.

Next turn Mega Metagross Bullet Punch (+1 priority) KOs Excadrill before it moves. If opponent instead switches Excadrill to Gengar-Mega, Dark Pulse lands super-effective (43-80%) and Metagross Psychic Fangs OHKOs Gengar-Mega next turn. This preserves Metagross as the Gengar-Mega answer while safely removing Excadrill's Sash.

Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball does 67-120% to Metagross (possible OHKO). Houndoom Flamethrower does 71-128% to Metagross. Combined = guaranteed KO. Gengar Energy Ball does 61-114% to Rotom-Wash (SE 2x, possible KO at 69%). Metagross Psychic Fangs guarantees KO on Gengar at 88%. Metagross Meteor Mash does only NVE 0.5x to Gengar (87-123% of max before type, ~44-62% after 0.5x, survives at 88%). Rotom Hydro Pump guaranteed OHKO on Houndoom. Wincon after Metagross falls: Gengar + Tyranitar vs Rotom 2v1, Gengar outspeeds at 200 and Energy Ball threatens KO.

decisions.rationale: Send in Tyranitar (38% HP) over Excadrill (4% HP). Next turn, Tyranitar's Helping Hand (priority +5) fires before Gengar's Energy Ball, boosting it to ~91-171% — guaranteed KO on Rotom-Wash at 63%. Excadrill's matchups into Rotom are poor (High Horsepower immune via Levitate, Iron Head NVE, Rock Slide neutral) and 4% HP is too fragile. Tyranitar is also Rock-type (immune to sand) and more durable. Dragapult at 15% is a permanent dead sack (LO recoil + sand > HP), so after Rotom falls it's a clean 2v0 win.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Gengar-Mega Energy Ball does 61-114% to Rotom-Wash (SE 2x). With Helping Hand (priority +5, 1.5x boost), Energy Ball becomes ~91-171% — guaranteed KO on Rotom at 63% HP. Tyranitar Helping Hand + Gengar Energy Ball is the cleanest wincon vs Rotom-Wash. Dragapult at 15% with Life Orb is permanently dead (10% LO + 6.25% sand = 16.25% > 15%). Shadow Tag locks opponent in. Excadrill at 4% has poor Rotom matchups: High Horsepower immune (Levitate), Iron Head NVE (0.5x), Rock Slide neutral only. Tyranitar at 38% is the superior bring. Sand has 3 turns remaining (sufficient).

decisions.rationale: Shadow Tag prevents switching and Volt Switch pivot. Metagross always outspeeds Houndoom (162 vs 126–161). Meteor Mash guarantees KO on Tyranitar (78.3–134.9%); Hydro Pump guarantees KO on Houndoom (90.1–169.3%). Both foes are removed this turn. The only counterplay is Tyranitar Helping Hand (+5 priority) boosting Houndoom's Flamethrower into a guaranteed OHKO on Metagross, but even then both foes fall and Rotom + Dragapult face Gengar-Mega + Excadrill with sand ticking down. If opponent forgoes Helping Hand, Metagross has a ~15% survival chance on Flamethrower's low roll, yielding a dominant position. Protect on Metagross is only ~50% reliable after consecutive use and risks losing with nothing gained. This line maximizes expected value against all opponent options.
decisions.notebook: Game 2, down 0-1. Opponent's sand core: Tyranitar (Smooth Rock, Impish), Excadrill (Focus Sash, Sand Rush), Houndoom (Life Orb, Flash Fire), Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag). Dragapult faints to Life Orb recoil afterward; Tyranitar's Crunch does 35–50.3% to Rotom-Wash, leaving it healthy enough to Hydro Pump Tyranitar next turn for the guaranteed KO. Loses only if Gengar-Mega Protects, but that is the opponent's less obvious line given the apparent Energy Ball OHKO on Rotom-Wash.

Protect Tyranitar to block Rotom-Wash's guaranteed Hydro Pump KO (Rotom outspeeds Tyranitar 106-138 vs 81, so Tyranitar would die before acting if it attacks). Excadrill Rock Slide chips Rotom to 24-39% before sandstorm drops it to ~18-33%. If Rotom attacks into Protect, both my Pokémon survive and Tyranitar Crunch (28.7-53.6%) guarantees KO next turn. If Rotom Protects, it's at 50.75% facing 2v1 with no sandstorm next turn — still heavily favorable. This dominates HH+Rock Slide (85% win if Rotom attacks) and Crunch+Rock Slide (~50% win if Rotom kills Tyranitar first).
decisions.notebook: Game 2 wincon confirmed: Tyranitar Helping Hand + Gengar-Mega Energy Ball guarantees KO on Rotom-Wash (91-171% with HH). Dragapult at 15% with Life Orb is permanently dead to LO+sand if it attacks. Shadow Tag traps both foes—no switches available anyway since Incineroar and Metagross are fainted. Endgame lesson: when facing a lone Rotom-Wash with Tyranitar (slow) + Excadrill (fast, sash spent), Protect Tyranitar to block Hydro Pump while Excadrill chips with Rock Slide—Rotom outspeeds Tyranitar so attacking with Tyranitar is strictly worse if Rotom targets it.

decisions.rationale: Hydro Pump OHKOs Tyranitar from 31%. Excadrill moves first (Sand Rush) and may Rock Slide for 17.8–26.1% with 30% flinch. If no flinch, Rotom KOs Tyranitar (speed tie determines whether Tyranitar gets a Crunch off first). The resulting 1v1 vs Excadrill is favourable: its attacks deal only ~10–26%, giving Rotom multiple Hydro Pump attempts. Targeting Tyranitar over Excadrill removes the bigger threat (Crunch 35–50.3%) and maximises survival odds.

Excadrill (Speed 140) outspeedes Rotom-Wash (106-138) and Rock Slides for 17.8-32.8% — 39% to KO from 27%. If it connects but doesn't KO, Rotom drops to 0.1-9.2% HP, creating a checkmate: Rotom's Hydro Pump (80% acc) KOs one of my Pokémon, but the survivor finishes — Excadrill outspeedes and Rock Slides for guaranteed KO from ≤9.2%, or Tyranitar Crunches for guaranteed KO (28.7-53.6%). Even if Excadrill misses (10%), Rotom must hit Hydro Pump on Tyranitar (80%) and then Excadrill still has a 39% shot next turn. ~94% win probability, strictly superior to Helping Hand which leaves Tyranitar unable to attack and removes the double-threat checkmate.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 endgame confirmed: Excadrill retains Speed 140 even without active sand (Sand Rush speed stat persists in engine). Tyranitar Crunch is guaranteed KO on Rotom-Wash from 27% (28.7-53.6%). Excadrill Rock Slide does 17.8-32.8% to Rotom-Wash (neutral, spread 0.75x). The Crunch+Rock Slide double-attack creates a checkmate vs a single Rotom-Wash: even if Rock Slide doesn't KO, the survivor always finishes. For game 3 if needed: same core Gengar-Mega+Tyranitar+Houndoom+Excadrill; opponent may adapt to HH+Energy Ball pattern — consider Shadow Ball on predicted Rotom Protect turns. Key lesson: when two attackers both threaten KO on a lone foe, double-attack is superior to Helping Hand because it preserves the checkmate property (survivor always finishes).

decisions.rationale: Hydro Pump into Tyranitar is the only winning path. If Tyranitar speed ≤107, Rotom moves first and KOs it; Excadrill's unboosted Rock Slide maxes at 26.1% and cannot KO Rotom from 27%, so Rotom survives and KOs Excadrill next turn. If Tyranitar speed ≥109 and uses Crunch, Rotom faints regardless of target choice. Protect only delays the same speed tie without improving odds. Hydro Pump into Excadrill always loses because Tyranitar Crunch KOs Rotom. Volt Switch fails to KO Tyranitar. The 80% accuracy is unavoidable risk.

reflections.summary: Series won 2-0. Game 2 was a fast 9-turn affair decided by favorable trades and two luck swings: a critical-hit Rock Slide that KO'd Incineroar on turn 2 (it was at 3% from the crit alone, effectively removing the opponent's Fake Out/Intimidate pivot early) and a Metagross Meteor Mash miss on turn 6 that let Houndoom survive to KO Metagross with Flamethrower. The sand core of Tyranitar+Excadrill closed out the endgame cleanly: Tyranitar Protect blocked Rotom's Hydro Pump on turn 8, then Excadrill's Rock Slide finished Rotom on turn 9. The one clear misplay was turn 7 Helping Hand into Gengar—Gengar fainted to Dragapult Shadow Ball before using the boosted move, costing the slot unnecessarily; a double-attack would have been strictly better. Team preview was strong: Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag plus Tyranitar sand and Excadrill sash created pressure the opponent couldn't answer, and Houndoom's Fire STAB was the correct Metagross answer.
reflections.adjustment: In a future series, keep the Gengar-Mega + Tyranitar + Excadrill + Houndoom core against this opponent—it matched up well. Fix the turn-7 type of error: when two attackers both threaten KO on a lone foe, double-attack instead of Helping Hand so the survivor always finishes. Consider Shadow Ball on predicted Rotom Protect turns rather than committing Helping Hand. The opponent may adapt to the sand+Shadow Tag pattern, so have a backup plan if they lead differently.
reflections.notebook: Opponent tendencies: brings 4 of 6 from Dragapult/Incineroar/Metagross-Mega/Rotom-Wash/Klefki/Serperior; tends to lead Incineroar+Rotom-Wash. Rotom-Wash runs Dark Pulse (not a standard utility set). Metagross-Mega is Adamant Meteor Mash/Psychic Fangs/Bullet Punch/Protect. Incineroar is Chople Berry Careful. Dragapult is Timid Life Orb Shadow Ball/Thunderbolt/Fire Blast/Protect. Klefki and Serperior were left on the bench both games—opponent may not value screens or Serperior against this roster. Strategic facts: Excadrill Sand Rush speed persists even after sand ends in this engine. Tyranitar Crunch + Excadrill Rock Slide is a guaranteed checkmate vs lone Rotom-Wash. Opponent does not protect-swap aggressively into predicted double targets. Prep conclusions: the registered six (Mega Gengar, Tyranitar, Excadrill, Gholdengo, Paldean Tauros Aqua, Houndoom) fit this opponent well; the four brought were optimal. Left-behind options (Grimmsnarl, Vaporeon, Hydrapple, Rotom) were not needed. Houndoom as the Metagross-Mega answer worked despite its fragility—Metagross must be removed before it can sweep.

reflections.summary: We lost the series 0-2 because our team lacked consistent answers to the opponent's Shadow Tag Gengar-Mega + sand core. In game 2, early flinch hax on Incineroar and a crucial Meteor Mash miss on Gengar-Mega prevented us from executing our plan. Even without the hax, the opponent's trapping and speed control overwhelmed our pivots and limited our offensive windows. The between-game adjustment to preserve Rotom-Wash and use Dragapult only after Gengar was removed was sound in theory, but in practice it left us unable to deal with Gengar-Mega efficiently and made us vulnerable to bad luck.
reflections.adjustment: In a future series, I would bring Klefki for Thunder Wave and screens to disrupt the opponent's speed advantage and reduce chip damage. I would drop Serperior and maybe swap Incineroar's item or spread, but keeping Intimidate and Fake Out is still valuable. I would avoid leading Incineroar into Gengar+Tyranitar to prevent early flinch KOs, and I would ensure Dragapult is positioned to snipe Gengar-Mega before it can trap key threats.
reflections.notebook: Opponent relies on a Shadow Tag Gengar-Mega + sand core (Tyranitar Smooth Rock, Excadrill Sash, Houndoom Life Orb). Gengar-Mega outspeeds everything but Dragapult and blocks all switching and pivot moves. Tyranitar is Impish physically bulky, Excadrill is fast under sand, Houndoom absorbs Fire moves. Our team must handle trapping without safe escapes. Rotom-Wash is our best Tyranitar/Excadrill answer but cannot 1v2 them. Dragapult is the only reliable OHKO on Gengar-Mega; preserve it for that purpose. Metagross can OHKO Gengar but is slower and risks Protect or hax. Klefki is essential for future series—Thunder Wave cripples both Gengar-Mega and Excadrill, while screens blunt Rock Slide flinch and Crunch damage. Consider leading Rotom + Metagross to pressure sand, with Klefki in back for speed control. Avoid bringing Serperior again; it is too slow into sand teams.
